- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative or volatile (especially after recent spikes).  
- Underestimate sharp downward moves when sentiment turns negative mid-cycle; model tends to lag in confirming sell-off momentum.  
- Overshoot after positive sentiment spikes — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects downward.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model often overcorrects from recent highs/lows, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish, then underestimating late periods (last 5–7 days) when sentiment turns bearish.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast amplitude by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in rebound.  
- If sentiment shows a clear reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to account for lagged market reaction.
